```{r}
# Import Packages
library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)
library(tidyverse) 
```

```{r}
library(tidyverse)

# 1. Load Data
fpkm <- read.csv("fpkm.csv", check.names = FALSE)
meta <- read.csv("MetaDataSheet.csv", check.names = FALSE)

# 2. Separate Expression and Transpose
# The notebook uses: df = dfo.iloc[:,8:].T
# This skips the first 8 metadata columns and makes samples the rows
expression_raw <- t(fpkm[, 9:ncol(fpkm)])
colnames(expression_raw) <- fpkm[, 1] # Set Transcript IDs as column names

# 3. Research-Specific Gene Filtering (_subset_genes logic)
# Note: The notebook code cells use thresholds of 5.0, not 1.0 or 2.0.
subset_min <- 5.0
subset_fold <- 5.0
eps <- 0.001 # Used in the notebook to prevent division by zero

# Selection criteria are calculated on non-log FPKM
max_vals <- apply(expression_raw, 2, max)
min_vals <- apply(expression_raw, 2, min)
# "mvt[ mvt<eps ] = eps" from the notebook:
min_vals[min_vals < eps] <- eps
fold_change <- max_vals / min_vals

# Identify genes that meet BOTH criteria
keep_genes <- which(max_vals > subset_min & fold_change > subset_fold)
expression_filtered <- expression_raw[, keep_genes]

# 4. Log Transformation
# The notebook uses: np.log2(data + 1)
X_log <- log2(expression_filtered + 1)

# 5. Metadata Integration (Research-Grade Labels)
# The notebook parses the 'Tracking ID' from the sample name and looks it up in meta
labels <- data.frame(Sample_FullName = rownames(X_log)) %>%
  mutate(Tracking_ID = str_extract(Sample_FullName, "^[^_]+")) %>%
  left_join(meta %>% mutate(`Tracking ID` = as.character(`Tracking ID`)), 
            by = c("Tracking_ID" = "Tracking ID")) %>%
  mutate(
    # Replicate notebook's age parsing (fw/nb/da/yr)
    Age_Numeric = case_when(
      str_detect(tolower(Age), "fw") ~ as.numeric(str_extract(Age, "\\d+")),
      str_detect(tolower(Age), "(nb|da)") ~ 0,
      str_detect(tolower(Age), "yr") ~ as.numeric(str_extract(Age, "\\d+")),
      TRUE ~ NA_real_
    ),
    Condition = tolower(Condition),
    Gender = tolower(Gender)
  )

# 6. Final Cleaned Dataset
# Combine the labels and the filtered, log-transformed expression data
fpkm_cleaned <- cbind(labels[, c("Tracking_ID", "Age_Numeric", "Gender", "Condition")], X_log)
```

```{r}
pca_out <- prcomp(fpkm_cleaned[, 5:ncol(fpkm_cleaned)], center = TRUE, scale. = TRUE)

pca_features <- data.frame(pca_out$x[, 1:2]) %>%
  bind_cols(fpkm_cleaned[, 1:4])

train_data <- pca_features %>% filter(Condition == "normal")
hgps_data  <- pca_features %>% filter(Condition == "hgps")
```



```{r}
library(caret)
library(neuralnet)

# 1. Scaling the PC data
# Neural networks work best when inputs are between 0 and 1 or -1 and 1.
# We'll use caret's preProcess to scale our training and progeria data.
preProcValues <- preProcess(train_data[, c("PC1", "PC2")], method = c("center", "scale"))

train_scaled <- predict(preProcValues, train_data)
hgps_scaled  <- predict(preProcValues, hgps_data)

# 2. Set up Cross-Validation control
ctrl <- trainControl(method = "cv", number = 10)

# 3. Train the Neural Network with a higher 'threshold' and 'stepmax'
# threshold: higher value (0.1) makes it easier to converge
# stepmax: allows the model more "tries" to find the answer
set.seed(42)
nn_clock <- train(Age_Numeric ~ PC1 + PC2, 
                  data = train_scaled, 
                  method = "neuralnet", 
                  trControl = ctrl,
                  tuneGrid = expand.grid(layer1 = 5, 
                                         layer2 = 0, 
                                         layer3 = 0),
                  linear.output = TRUE,
                  threshold = 0.1,  
                  stepmax = 1e6)

# Check the results again
print(nn_clock)
```

```{r}
# 1. Get the predictions from your NN model
predictions <- predict(nn_clock, train_scaled)

# 2. Calculate the Absolute Errors (the "distance" for each person)
abs_errors <- abs(train_scaled$Age_Numeric - predictions)

# 3. Calculate Mean (MAE) and Median (MedAE)
mae_val <- mean(abs_errors)
med_ae_val <- median(abs_errors)

# 4. Print the results clearly
cat("--- Performance Metrics ---\n")
cat("Mean Absolute Error (MAE):   ", round(mae_val, 2), " years\n")
cat("Median Absolute Error (MedAE):", round(med_ae_val, 2), " years\n")
```






```{r}
# 1. Get predictions from the NN model
nn_preds <- predict(nn_clock, train_scaled)

# 2. Create a results dataframe
nn_results <- data.frame(Actual = train_scaled$Age_Numeric, 
                         Predicted = nn_preds)

# 3. Plot
ggplot(nn_results, aes(x = Actual, y = Predicted)) +
  geom_point(color = "darkgreen", alpha = 0.5) +
  geom_abline(intercept = 0, slope = 1, linetype = "dashed", color = "red") +
  labs(title = "Neural Network: Predicted vs. Actual Age",
       subtitle = paste("MAE:", round(mean(abs(nn_results$Actual - nn_results$Predicted)), 2)),
       x = "Chronological Age (Years)",
       y = "Predicted Biological Age (Years)") +
  theme_minimal()
```

```{r}
# Plotting the difference (Error) against Actual Age
ggplot(nn_results, aes(x = Actual, y = Predicted - Actual)) +
  geom_point() +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0, color ="cornflowerblue") +
  labs(
       x = "Chronological Age", y = "Error") +

```

```{r}
library(ggplot2)
library(dplyr)

# 1. Extract PC1 loadings (rotation)
pc1_data <- data.frame(GeneID = rownames(pca_results$rotation), 
                       Loading = pca_results$rotation[, "PC1"])

# 2. Add an "Direction" column and filter for the Top 20
top_loadings <- pc1_data %>%
  mutate(AbsLoading = abs(Loading),
         Direction = ifelse(Loading > 0, "Increasing", "Decreasing")) %>%
  arrange(desc(AbsLoading)) %>%
  slice(1:20) # Take the top 20

# 3. Create the Dot Plot
ggplot(top_loadings, aes(x = AbsLoading, y = reorder(GeneID, AbsLoading))) +
  # Draw a horizontal line behind the point for style
  # Add the points, colored by direction
  geom_point(size = 2) +
    # Add titles and labels
  labs(
       x = "Absolute Gene Weight",
       y = "Gene Identifier") +
  theme_minimal()
# Save the plot
ggsave("Top_Aging_Drivers_PC1.png", width = 8, height = 7, dpi = 300)
```





```{r}
# 1. Calculate the percentage of variance explained
pca_var <- pca_out$sdev^2
pca_var_perc <- (pca_var / sum(pca_var)) * 100

# 2. Create a data frame for the first 10 components
scree_df <- data.frame(
  PC = 1:10, 
  Variance = pca_var_perc[1:10]
)

# 3. Generate the Scree Line Plot
ggplot(scree_df, aes(x = PC, y = Variance)) +
  geom_line(color = "cornflowerblue") +      # The main line
  geom_point(color = "black") +            # Individual points for each PC
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = 1:10) +              # Ensure every PC number is shown
  labs(
       x = "Principal Component", 
       y = "Variance Explained") +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(panel.grid.minor = element_blank())
```

  max_depth = c(3, 4, 5),     # Allow more complex interactions

)

  Age_Numeric ~ PC1 + PC2,
  data = train_scaled,
  method = "xgbTree",
  trControl = loocv_ctrl,
  tuneGrid = xgb_grid_v2,

)

```{r}
library(ggplot2)
library(patchwork)

# 1. Ultra-clean theme function
minimal_age_theme <- function() {
  list(
    # Points are now black, line is blue
    geom_point(color = "black", alpha = 0.4, size = 1.5), 
    geom_smooth(method = "lm", formula = y ~ x, color = "cornflowerblue", fill = "lightblue", se = TRUE, linewidth = 1),
    geom_abline(intercept = 0, slope = 1, linetype = "dotted", color = "gray60"),
    scale_x_continuous(limits = c(0, 100)),
    scale_y_continuous(limits = c(0, 100)),
    theme_classic(),
    theme(
      # Normal (unbold) titles
      plot.title = element_text(hjust = 0.5, face = "plain", size = 12),
      axis.line = element_line(color = "black"),
      panel.grid = element_blank(),
      axis.title = element_text(size = 10)
    )
  )
}

# 2. Build the Neural Network Plot
p_nn <- ggplot(data.frame(x = train_scaled$Age_Numeric, y = as.numeric(nn_preds)), aes(x, y)) +
  minimal_age_theme() +
  labs(title = "Neural Network", y = "Predicted age", x = "True age")

# 3. Build the XGBoost Plot
p_xgb <- ggplot(data.frame(x = train_scaled$Age_Numeric, y = as.numeric(xgb_preds)), aes(x, y)) +
  minimal_age_theme() +
  labs(title = "XGBoost", y = "", x = "True age") +
  theme(axis.text.y = element_blank(), axis.ticks.y = element_blank())

# 4. Combine side-by-side
p_nn | p_xgb
```


```{r}
# 1. Prepare the High-Dimensional Data
# Get the names of the top 100 genes from your previous PCA analysis
top_gene_names <- names(sort(abs(pca_results$rotation[, "PC1"]), decreasing = TRUE)[1:100])

# 2. Filter and Clean
nn_data_full <- fpkm_cleaned %>%
  filter(Condition == "healthy") %>%
  # Keep only Age and our Top 100 biological drivers
  select(Age_Numeric, all_of(top_gene_names)) %>%
  # Final safety check for NAs
  drop_na()

# 3. Scaling is MANDATORY for Neural Nets
# We scale all 100 genes so they are on the same "playing field"
preProcFull <- preProcess(nn_data_full %>% select(-Age_Numeric), method = c("center", "scale"))
nn_data_scaled <- predict(preProcFull, nn_data_full)

# 4. Train the "Biological" Neural Network
# We use a single layer of 5-10 nodes to prevent overfitting
set.seed(42)
nn_full_clock <- train(Age_Numeric ~ ., 
                       data = nn_data_scaled, 
                       method = "neuralnet", 
                       trControl = trainControl(method = "cv", number = 10),
                       tuneGrid = expand.grid(layer1 = 8, layer2 = 0, layer3 = 0),
                       linear.output = TRUE,
                       threshold = 0.5, # Higher threshold helps with high-dimensional convergence
                       stepmax = 1e6)

print(nn_full_clock)
```



```{r}
library(xgboost)
library(caret)

# 1. Filter for Healthy Donors (as we did for the PCA and NN models)
# This ensures we are measuring "Normal Aging" first
xgb_data_full <- fpkm_cleaned %>%
  filter(Condition == "healthy") %>%
  filter(!is.na(Age_Numeric)) %>%
  select(-Tracking_ID, -Gender, -Condition) # Remove metadata, keep Age + Genes

# 2. Set up LOOCV
loocv_ctrl <- trainControl(method = "LOOCV")

# 3. Define a grid that prevents overfitting on high dimensions
# With 4,000 genes, we use 'colsample_bytree' to force the model
# to look at different subsets of genes for each tree.
xgb_full_grid <- expand.grid(
  nrounds = 150,           # More trees to handle the complexity
  max_depth = 3,           # Shallow trees to prevent memorization
  eta = 0.05,              # Slow learning rate for stability
  gamma = 1,               # Penalty for unnecessary complexity
  colsample_bytree = 0.3,  # Each tree only looks at 30% of the genes
  min_child_weight = 1,
  subsample = 0.8          # Each tree looks at 80% of samples
)

# 4. Train the Model (This will take longer than the PCA version)
set.seed(42)
xgb_full_model <- train(
  Age_Numeric ~ .,
  data = xgb_data_full,
  method = "xgbTree",
  trControl = loocv_ctrl,
  tuneGrid = xgb_full_grid,
  verbosity = 0
)

# 5. Review the results
print(xgb_full_model)

# 6. Extract the "Biological Heroes" (Top Features)
importance <- varImp(xgb_full_model, scale = FALSE)
plot(importance, top = 20, main = "Top Genetic Predictors (Full Transcriptome)")
```

library(tidyverse)

# 1. Create a clean training set
# We filter for healthy donors and drop the non-numeric metadata
xgb_ready_data <- fpkm_cleaned %>%
  filter(Condition == "healthy") %>%
  select(-Tracking_ID, -Gender, -Condition) %>%
  # THE FIX: Drop any column (gene) that has an NA value
  select_if(~ !any(is.na(.))) 

# 2. Safety Verification
# This should print 0. If it doesn't, check your Age_Numeric column for NAs.
print(paste("Missing values remaining:", sum(is.na(xgb_ready_data))))

# 3. Check the "Survivors"
# This tells you how many genes are left to train on
print(dim(xgb_ready_data))

```{r}
library(tidyverse)

# 1. The Clean Sweep
# We start with your full dataset and aggressively prune NAs
nn_final_data <- fpkm_cleaned %>%
  # Keep only healthy samples
  filter(Condition == "healthy") %>%
  # Ensure Age_Numeric itself isn't missing
  filter(!is.na(Age_Numeric)) %>%
  # Remove the metadata strings
  select(-Tracking_ID, -Gender, -Condition) %>%
  # DROP GENES: If a gene has even ONE missing value, delete the whole gene column
  select(where(~ !any(is.na(.))))

# 2. THE DIAGNOSTIC (Check your console after running)
cat("--- DATA CLEANING REPORT ---\n")
cat("Final Samples (Rows): ", nrow(nn_final_data), "\n")
cat("Final Genes (Columns): ", ncol(nn_final_data), "\n")
cat("Total NA values remaining: ", sum(is.na(nn_final_data)), "\n")

# 3. IF THE COUNT ABOVE IS 0, PROCEED TO MODEL:
if(sum(is.na(nn_final_data)) == 0) {
  
  # Select the Top 100 Genes for the NN (using your previous PCA results)
  top_gene_names <- names(sort(abs(pca_results$rotation[, "PC1"]), decreasing = TRUE)[1:100])
  
  # Ensure these top genes actually exist in our cleaned data
  available_genes <- intersect(top_gene_names, colnames(nn_final_data))
  
  nn_ready <- nn_final_data %>% 
    select(Age_Numeric, all_of(available_genes))
  
  # Scale and Train
  preProcFull <- preProcess(nn_ready %>% select(-Age_Numeric), method = c("center", "scale"))
  nn_scaled <- predict(preProcFull, nn_ready)
  
  set.seed(42)
  nn_full_clock <- train(
    Age_Numeric ~ ., 
    data = nn_scaled, 
    method = "neuralnet", 
    trControl = trainControl(method = "cv", number = 10),
    tuneGrid = expand.grid(layer1 = 5, layer2 = 0, layer3 = 0),
    linear.output = TRUE,
    threshold = 0.5,
    stepmax = 1e6
  )
  
  print(nn_full_clock)
  
} else {
  stop("Data still contains NAs! Check your Age_Numeric column specifically.")
}
```
